title: The account-date and holiday reads and the deviation pause have no published surface in the target
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8 and 10; Ownership Map v1 (api rows for P1 rwb-source-data and S8 rwb-deviation); legacy story RWB-E1-028 sections 3, 4, 12; FSD P3 v4 A2.11 and A2.12
section: s3 Preconditions; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.4 Events consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes
description: The story sets the prescription date from the last payment date and the contract date of the linked accounts and counts service levels in working days from the holiday calendar, so it needs two reads of another service. Architecture v5 slide 10 names GET /accounts/{id} on rwb-source-data and slide 8 keeps the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views read only by rwb-source-data, but no source gives the account-date read of a set of linked accounts, the data-as-of field, or a holiday read at all, so the consumed rows, the fake and the AC3 and AC6 mocks cannot be fixed. The same section needs the deviation pause: AC10 is driven by DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared, S8 is wave 2, and the assigned dependency set of this story carries no S8 contract story, so the wave 1 path is not stated either.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10: rwb-source-data GET /v1/customers/{id}, /accounts/{id}; slide 8: 30 recovery.v_ace_* views read only by rwb-source-data; legacy RWB-E1-028 section 12: RecoveryDataQuery.accountDates(List<UUID>) and holidays(LocalDate, LocalDate), both 'P1, used by this story'; TSD P3 v3 T2.3 gives no P1 path; RWB-ITG-E1028-ITG resolves the wave 1 pause through the P3 case action contract.
proposed: Add the two P1 rows to the Ownership Map with their query and answer shape, and record in the P3 contract which operation carries the wave 1 pause; until then read the account dates and the calendar behind the P1 contract at the two paths of section 12.2 and prove AC10 against the rwb-deviation contract mock.

title: No source gives the field-level detail of the two escalation columns or of the TimerBreached payload
source: Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD P3 v3 section T3.1 (timer DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-041); Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8; legacy story RWB-E1-028 sections 11 and 12; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42
section: s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.3 Events published; s11 Data
description: The timer story writes the escalation the legacy story raised, but neither the TSD timer table nor the data dictionary has a row for escalated_to_role or escalated_at: DF-WRK-043 and DF-WRK-044 are allocated by the case record view story RWB-P3-E2015-APP only, and no source fixes their type, length or optionality. The TimerBreached payload is fixed by the catalogue as event 19 on rwb.case.events.v1 with caseId as the key but its field list (legacy EV-19 gives timerId, caseId, escalateTo) does not name caseNo, timerType or expiresAt, so the baseline cannot publish a schema without assuming which fields are carried.
evidence: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 timer rows end at warn_at, paused, status and escalation level; RWB-E1-028 section 12 lists TimerBreached (EV-19: timerId, caseId, escalateTo) and TimerDue (EV-18); Architecture v5 slide 42 gives TimerBreached as event 19 and TimerDue as retired with no payload field list; RWB-P3-E2015-APP section 11 states DF-WRK-043 and DF-WRK-044 arrive with this story's migration.
proposed: Add the two escalation columns and the TimerBreached payload to the logical model and the event catalogue, and settle the field-level detail in the baseline review of RWB-P3-E1028-CON.

title: No source gives the operational values for a durable timer: poll window, catch-up window, breach band and record-failure rate
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 28 and 44; legacy story RWB-E1-028 sections 5 and 13; TSD P3 v3 T2.3
section: s13 Solution plan (alert mapping); s14 Validation and messages; s11 Data
description: The deployment alerts on a worker that stopped polling, on a timer that stayed unmet after a restart, on the TimerBreached volume and on the MSG-P7-003 rate, but no source gives a threshold, a window or a band. The legacy story names only a five-minute job cadence and one parameter, legal.prescription.warn.days = 180, and both belong to the business rules and not to the deployment; the target retires the job, so the five-minute figure cannot be reused as a poll window without inventing a value.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44: JOB-21 stuck workflow scan every 5 min, visibility query + alert; slide 28: stuck-case alert and the daily ledger anchor; FSD P3 v4 A2.11 to A2.13 give no operational value; TSD P3 v3 T2.3 gives the run cadence only.
proposed: Set the four values in the rwb-case values files, confirm them at UAT and record the agreed values in the runbook entry each alert links.
